details_checked: Exact provider/type key and pinned registry-version resolution before classification
Registry-authorized intent-specific projection overrides, e.g. logging service inspector-only in Runtime but node in Operations
Multiple association badges referencing one authoritative resource ID without creating copied resources

Validation and failure behavior: invalid targets, cardinality, cycles, arbitrary edges, selector/inheritance evidence, redaction/pin-policy violations, registry lookup and provider evaluation fallbacks
View-switch losslessness, layout persistence per intent/layer, and handling of unrepresentable changes
Unknown, unsupported, imported, child, ephemeral, and offline resource handling plus safe unclassified pins
Migration preview classes, stop conditions, resource-count/identity invariants, journaled rollback
Keyboard, screen-reader, non-color, zoom/density, and focus stability behavior
Rollout gates, metrics, and stop/rollback conditions
implementation_options: A: every resource as a node — rejected for false topology and unusable density
B: provider-curated visible allowlist — rejected as the architecture; retained as evidence-backed registry metadata
C: universal semantic taxonomy — retained as the core rendering contract bounded by provider adapters, confidence, and honest fallback
D: diagram-purpose presets/layers — retained as the projection mechanism, not standalone hard-coded filtering
E: separate inventory from canvas — retained with one shared identity and locate/reveal links
F: user-controlled visibility/pinning — rejected as primary rule; retained only as safe labelled documentation pins
G: registry plus intent-based projections — selected as the governing approach
vote.proposed_artifact: Accepted unchanged. Concise restatement: one authoritative resource inventory; diagrams are intent-specific projections resolved through a pinned, provider-validated semantic registry; only topology-relevant resources render as nodes; scopes, attachments, policies, relationships, child details, operational/metadata resources, and documentation pins have distinct representations or inventory-only fallback; unknown/unsupported types stay visible but blocked from auto-placement; view switching and pins never mutate resource truth; configured/effective states carry provenance; migration is previewed, journaled, and reversible; accessibility and rollout stop conditions are mandatory.
requirements_covered: Maintain one authoritative inventory per resource identity; diagrams never own or duplicate resource records
Render each architecture diagram as an intent-specific projection driven by validated resource semantics
Only topology-relevant resources become nodes; scopes, attachments, policies, relationships, details, and documentation pins receive distinct representations or inventory-only treatment
Distinguish configured, effective, stale, pending, unknown, and unsupported states with provenance and timestamps
Keep unknown, unsupported, imported, child, ephemeral, and offline resources visible and searchable with safe fallback and no fabricated relationships
Ensure view switches, layers, and pins never create, attach, edit, or delete provider resources
Provide migration preview, identity/resource-count invariants, journaled rollback, and legacy projection preservation
Require accessibility, non-color encoding, keyboard/command alternatives, and defined density/zoom behavior for every renderer and action
vote.summary: Candidate v0 satisfies the stated decision scope: it separates authoritative resource inventory from intent-specific projections, uses a provider-validated semantic taxonomy with honest fallback, keeps every diagram reference bound to a single resource identity, and defines safe pins, migration/rollback, validation, accessibility, and reversible rollout. No material in-scope omission, contradiction, or unsupported claim was found; retained unknowns are explicitly downstream P0/implementation items and scope exclusions.
